title: Linear Programming: Constraints, Feasible Regions and the Corner Point Method
seo_title: Linear Programming Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 12)
standard_text: Introduction, related terminology such as constraints, objective function, optimization; graphical method of solution for problems in two variables, feasible and infeasible regions (bounded or unbounded), feasible and infeasible solutions, optimal feasible solutions (up to three non-trivial constraints) (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Linear Programming worksheet (NCERT Chapter 12): objective functions, constraints, feasible points, corner points, the corner point method for maximum and minimum, and unbounded regions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The optimal value of Z occurs at a corner point.
key_sub: For an unbounded region, check the half-plane before accepting a corner value.
body_html:
How it works

  • An LPP maximises or minimises an objective function Z = ax + by subject to linear constraints and x, y ≥ 0.
  • The feasible region is the set of points that satisfy every constraint.
  • Corner point method: find the corner points (where boundary lines meet), work out Z at each, and pick the largest or smallest.
  • If the region is unbounded, the largest (smallest) corner value M is the maximum (minimum) only if the half-plane ax + by > M (< M) has no point in the region.
Example

Maximise Z = 3x + 4y with corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3), (0, 4).

Z = 0, 12, 18, 16

Answer: 18 at (2, 3)

Common mistakes

  • Writing the inequality the wrong way round.
  • Swapping the coefficients of x and y in a constraint.
  • Assuming a maximum always exists in an unbounded region.

faq.a: For a linear Z, the optimum of a bounded region is always at a corner.

faq.q: Can there be more than one optimal point?
faq.a: Yes. If two corners give the same optimum, every point between them does too.

items.q: In a linear programming problem, where does the optimal value of Z occur (if it exists)?
c: At the centre of the feasible region
At a corner point of the feasible region
items.e: At a corner point of the feasible region.

items.q: What are the conditions x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 called?
items.e: Non-negative constraints.

items.q: A factory makes x fans and y lamps. Each of the fans needs 4 hours of assembly and each of the lamps needs 5 hours. At most 113 hours of assembly are available. Which constraint is correct?
items.e: Hours used = 4x + 5y, and it cannot be more than 113: 4x + 5y ≤ 113.

items.q: A factory makes x kurtas and y shirts. Each of the kurtas needs 6 hours of tailoring and each of the shirts needs 1 hour. At most 65 hours of tailoring are available. Which constraint is correct?
items.e: Hours used = 6x + 1y, and it cannot be more than 65: 6x + y ≤ 65.

items.q: A factory makes x chairs and y tables. Each of the chairs needs 1 hour of carpentry and each of the tables needs 6 hours. At most 104 hours of carpentry are available. Which constraint is correct?
items.e: Hours used = 1x + 6y, and it cannot be more than 104: x + 6y ≤ 104.

items.q: Two corner points give the same maximum value of Z. Which is true?
c: Only those two points give the maximum
Every point on the segment joining them also gives the maximum
items.e: Every point on the segment joining them also gives the maximum.
